rites.name: Ilotamira
rites.text: Ilotamira is the concept of resonance that Ryeralwen gave itself in the Singing, when the first roots of the world condensed out of sound. It is less a being than a pattern of tones that holds nascent matter in place until it can settle into form.

rites.name: Xaeshora
rites.text: Xaeshora is a concept of Ryeralwen, a principle of binding and threshold that the Courts of the second age used to seal the doors between worlds. Its power was felt in councils and divine trials, where its presence marked the moment an oath became law.

rites.name: Suralanuta
rites.text: Suralanuta is a concept of the Ryeralwen Arcane realm, understood as the unifying principle by which the Courts of the Second Era bound their councils and trials to one another. During the Age of Sundering, the concept was invoked to seal the doors between worlds whenever landfall threatened to break old oaths.

rites.name: Ameornium
rites.text: Ameornium is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Ryeralwen, a quiet principle the makers wove into the Weave during the Seeding, when latent powers were laid to sleep. In the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds between peoples, it was invoked as a theory of how severed ties might be mended.

rites.name: Crodath
rites.text: Crodath is the concept of the Weave as it was planted during the Seeding, a slow pattern of binding that the makers laid into the air of Ryeralwen. In the Age of Sundering its strands were torn loose by landfall, and the quiet powers it had held began to wake in scattered, uneven ways.
